classification.difficultyReason: The partial-fraction identity is supplied; separation and two population observations determine the carrying capacity.

content.prompt:
A town’s population $P$ satisfies
$$\frac{dP}{dt}=0.04P\left(\frac{C-P}{C}\right),$$
where $t$ is years after 2005 and $C$ is the carrying capacity.

In 2005 the population was $40\,000$; in 2025 it was $70\,000$.

Use $\dfrac{C}{P(C-P)}=\dfrac{1}{P}+\dfrac{1}{C-P}$ to find the carrying capacity, to the nearest thousand.

answer.worked:
Separating variables and using the supplied identity,
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{C}{P(C-P)}\,dP&=0.04\,dt\\
\int\left(\frac1P+\frac1{C-P}\right)\,dP&=\int0.04\,dt\\
\ln P-\ln(C-P)&=0.04t+k\\
\ln\left(\frac{P}{C-P}\right)&=0.04t+k\\
\frac{P}{C-P}&=Ae^{0.04t}.
\end{align*}$$
The two data points give
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{40\,000}{C-40\,000}&=A\\
\frac{70\,000}{C-70\,000}&=Ae^{0.8}.
\end{align*}$$
Dividing eliminates $A$:
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{70\,000(C-40\,000)}{40\,000(C-70\,000)}&=e^{0.8}\\
\frac{7(C-40\,000)}{4(C-70\,000)}&=e^{0.8}\\
7(C-40\,000)&=4e^{0.8}(C-70\,000)\\
(4e^{0.8}-7)C&=280\,000(e^{0.8}-1)\\
C&=\frac{280\,000(e^{0.8}-1)}{4e^{0.8}-7}.
\end{align*}$$
The carrying capacity is therefore $180\,000$ people, to the nearest thousand.
